name: San Diego International Airport
before:
San Diego's airport, three miles north west of downtown, and the busiest single runway airport in the United States. It is a hub for Alaska Airlines and squeezes all of that onto 663 acres.

The approach is worth knowing about. Aircraft come in close to the skyscrapers of downtown and drop steeply over the crest of Bankers Hill, with shifting wind currents in the last moments and a relatively short usable landing area.

The practical consequence is delays. Almost all traffic uses Runway 27, because the winds usually come from the west. When Santa Ana winds blow from the east, or when the marine layer brings the cloud base down, operations reverse onto Runway 9, because Runway 27 has no instrument landing system and the terrain makes one infeasible. With only one taxiway running the length of the runway, those reversals back things up.

There are two terminals and 52 gates, with nine more due in Terminal 1 by 2028. Terminal 2's West concourse holds the international arrivals facility.
after:
San Diego's airport, three miles north west of downtown and the busiest single runway airport in the United States. It is a base for Alaska Airlines and squeezes all of that onto 663 acres.

The approach is worth knowing about. Aircraft come in close to the tall buildings of downtown on an unusually steep descent, onto a relatively short usable landing area.

There are two terminals. The first phase of the new Terminal 1 opened in September 2025, and the airport says the next phase will add 11 more gates by 2028.

claims.inAfter: It is a base for Alaska Airlines
claims.note: Was 'a hub for Alaska Airlines'. Alaska's own release of 3 September 2026 names Seattle and Honolulu as its largest hubs and says it is the only airline with both a pilot and a flight attendant base in the San Diego region; it also says it flies to more destinations from San Diego (50 with Loreto from December) than any other airline. By passengers Southwest is far bigger: BTS gives Southwest 35.89 per cent and Alaska 13.70 per cent for the twelve months to June 2026. 'Base' is what the airline itself says and what Wikipedia's 'hub' at least implies.

claims.claim: Santa Ana and marine-layer reversals; no ILS on Runway 27
claims.wasBefore: When Santa Ana winds blow from the east, or when the marine layer brings the cloud base down, operations reverse onto Runway 9, because Runway 27 has no instrument landing system and the terrain makes one infeasible.
claims.why: The reversals and their causes are Wikipedia alone. The FAA's current procedures confirm that only Runway 09 has ILS approaches (Runway 27 has a localizer and satellite approaches), but nothing read ties the reversals or delays to it, and 'infeasible' is Wikipedia alone. The airport's quarterly noise reports, which would show runway use, are encrypted PDFs the tools cannot read.

The FAA counted 12,675,684 boardings, 0.82 per cent down on 2024, so the record rests on the airport's total-passenger count.
